_comment: A workload that genuinely SPANS two participants.
Canton requires every actAs party of a submission to be hosted on the
submitting participant, so no single transaction can be co-signed by
parties on different nodes. Real apps span participants with propose/accept:
setup    the issuer (hosted on participant 1) creates PaymentOffers whose
counterparty is a party hosted on participant 2.
measured the counterparty ACCEPTS — a transaction submitted by a DIFFERENT
participant, against a contract created on the first one.
That measured transaction is what proves a real network: topology has
propagated, participant 2 can see participant 1's contract, and the commit
is coordinated through the shared synchronizer.
Run against the two-participant network (see examples/network/README.md):

setup._comment: Offers from the issuer on p1 to party 1, which round-robin placement hosts on p2.

_comment: Accepted by the recipient — actAsFrom reads 'to' off the offer, and that
party is hosted on participant 2, so this submission goes to a different
node than the one that created the contract.
